issues.t: CVT slipping, jerking or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car barely speeds up, it jerks or shakes when pulling away, or it suddenly loses power on the road. Some cars stop moving altogether.
issues.why: The continuously variable automatic (CVT) wears internally. GM gave dealers a bulletin on reading the metal debris on the CVT pan magnets to decide when the transmission must be replaced.
issues.next: Get it checked as soon as it starts slipping, and avoid highway driving until then because it can lose power without warning. Ask the dealer whether any warranty or bulletin coverage applies.

issues.t: Engine burns oil and loses compression
issues.sym: You have to add oil between changes, the check engine light comes on or flashes, and the engine shakes and loses power. Often found around 20,000 to 40,000 miles.
issues.why: On many early 1.2L engines, oil burning fouled the spark plugs and damaged valves, most often on cylinder 4. Compression tests showed one weak cylinder, and many engines were replaced. GM also did a PCV-related campaign on these cars.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up. If it keeps dropping or the light flashes, stop driving hard and ask a dealer for an oil consumption test and any open campaigns.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power or engine shutting off
issues.sym: The car loses power on the highway, warning lights flash on the dash, and the engine may die and not restart.
issues.why: Most reports trace back to the same oil burning and valve damage on the 1.2L engine, which leaves the engine unable to make power. Some cars needed a new engine.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have a compression test done to see if the engine is damaged.

issues.t: CVT whine or hesitation when pulling away
issues.sym: A whining sound that rises with speed, or a delay and stumble when you press the gas from a stop.
issues.why: Some whine and lag are normal for a CVT, but owners report these early on cars with the 1.4L engine. Fluid problems or internal wear can make them worse and lead to slipping.
issues.next: Note when the noise or delay happens and have the dealer check for codes and fluid condition while the car is under warranty or soon after.

issues.t: Coolant reservoir cracks and leaks
issues.sym: The coolant tank is low or empty, you smell coolant, or you see it dripping near the alternator. Usually around 40,000 to 55,000 miles.
issues.why: The plastic coolant reservoir cracks along its middle seam or at the hose inlet. Some replacement tanks have cracked again.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and watch the temperature gauge. Replace the tank before the engine runs low and overheats.

issues.t: A/C blows warm
issues.sym: The A/C cools on the highway but blows warm in traffic, cycles between cold and cool, or quits altogether.
issues.why: Owners report compressor leaks and failures, and GM ran a service campaign that added a sensor and low-pressure switch kit to the A/C system on these cars.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the A/C campaign was done on your VIN. Otherwise have the system checked for leaks before simply recharging it.

issues.t: Hood can open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood may pop up without warning while driving, blocking your view.
issues.why: The hood latch can corrode and stick, so the hood is not held down properly. GM issued two recalls for this (NHTSA 14V593000 and 22V640000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free repair. Until then, make sure the hood is firmly latched before each drive.

issues.t: Missing seat belt or key reminder chime (recall)
issues.sym: No chime sounds when the driver is unbuckled or when the key is left in the ignition.
issues.why: A software issue kept the warning chimes from sounding, which does not meet federal rules (NHTSA 16V257000 and 16V422000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the software for free.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front end, or in the worst case the wheel can move out of position and steering is lost.
issues.why: On a small number of cars the bolts holding the lower control arm to the steering knuckle were not tightened properly (NHTSA 14V440000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free dealer inspection done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: On a very small number of 2013 cars the front passenger airbag inflator may not work in a crash (NHTSA 14V298000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag risk to unbelted child (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The risk is a neck injury to an unbelted child in the front passenger seat if the airbag deploys.
issues.why: The front passenger airbag setup did not meet the federal standard for small occupants (NHTSA 17V307000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Always seat children in the back seat, belted.

issues.t: Airbags may not deploy from wrong setting (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs.
issues.why: A handful of 2019 cars had an incorrect airbag setting that could stop the airbags from deploying (NHTSA 18V774000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Misfire or rough running on cold start
issues.sym: The engine shakes or runs rough right after a cold start, and the check engine light may come on or flash.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for misfire codes on this engine, including code P050D (rough cold start) and spark plugs with a cracked center insulator.
issues.next: Have the codes read. New spark plugs, a coil or a software update are the usual fixes. A flashing light means you should drive gently and get it checked right away.

issues.t: Engine uses oil between changes
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, or the low oil warning comes on.
issues.why: Some 1.4L engines burn oil. GM has a bulletin for diagnosing oil consumption, which can come from piston rings or the PCV system.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and keep it full. If it uses more than a quart every 2,000 miles or so, ask the dealer for an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Check engine light for fuel vapor leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the car drives. You may have trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: A leak in the evaporative emissions system, such as a bad charcoal canister, purge valve or gas cap, sets codes like P0442 or P0455.
issues.next: Tighten the gas cap first. If the light stays on, a shop can smoke-test the system to find the leak.

issues.t: Fuel gauge stops working
issues.sym: The fuel gauge does not move or reads wrong, so you cannot tell how much gas is left.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel level sensor in the tank or its wiring.
issues.next: Track mileage with the trip meter to avoid running out, and have the sensor tested.

issues.t: Radio stays on or speakers crackle
issues.sym: The radio keeps playing after the car is turned off, or the speakers crackle or cut out.
issues.why: Faults in the radio unit, its software or the speaker wiring.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about radio software updates. A radio that stays on can drain the battery, so get it checked.

issues.t: Front brakes wear quickly in city driving
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding when braking, or a pedal that feels less firm.
issues.why: Stop-and-go city driving wears the front pads and rotors faster on this small car.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at each tire rotation and replace the pads before they wear down to the rotors.

issues.t: "Propulsion power is reduced" warning (Spark EV)
issues.sym: A "Propulsion power is reduced" message appears and the car slows down, sometimes to a stop. It may also refuse to charge.
issues.why: A failing cell in the high-voltage battery pack. The dealer replaced the bad cell in the reported case.
issues.next: Get off the road safely and have the car towed to a Chevrolet EV dealer. Ask about the high-voltage battery warranty.

issues.t: Brake warning and weak brake pedal (Spark EV)
issues.sym: Brake, ABS, traction or "Service brake assist" lights come on, and the brake pedal gets hard or goes down with little stopping power.
issues.why: Owners report faults in the electronic brake system on the Spark EV. Dealers suspected wheel speed sensors or the brake control computer, but no single fix has been confirmed.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Stop driving if the brake warning lights come on. Have the car towed to a dealer and ask them to check for software updates.
